title: release resume across local midnight refuses its own release commit
body:
A cut that fails before its tag and is resumed after local midnight refuses its own stamped release commit ("a released note is never re-dated"), and only a reset of the unpushed release commit gets past it; seen on 0.1.27 (015b2fa5, 2026-11-17), re-cut from c6f6a745 and tagged at 9cd0fbbd.

## Resolution

Fixed by unit 0372-1, landed at 73d60f09, for the next batch cut (written 2026-11-18 15:03Z by date -u).

Pre-flight (lib/cmd/release) asks notes_check about the note's own day, not today, when HEAD is already the release commit: the stamp is in it, the tree is clean, and the tag is absent here and on every remote, since pre-flight already refuses a remote's tag this checkout lacks. The stamp step does not run for such a commit, so nothing is re-dated. A note not yet dated is checked against today as before, and a note a tag released is never checked there, since that cut resumes past the tag. A pushed release always carries its tag, so it needs no check of its own.

Proof: cc's run on the Desk (slot 01M7QJ7W42QKZS0Q2WZK0VBR2Z, 14:51Z to 15:01Z). releasecut.bats's new arm cuts to the tag step on one day and resumes on the next; it was red at the base, pre-flight refusing its own release commit with "a released note is never re-dated", and green at the tip, where releasecut.bats whole passed under BSD and GNU (234 of 234 each), with `bin/devbin test scans` (61 of 61) and `bin/devbin check lint` (0 breaches). The record is in ~/Devel/scratch/devbin-cc/i0372/runs/.
